visual_brief.subject: OpenAI explains how Habitat returned to multi-tenancy at global scale
verified_context: OpenAI describes Habitat moving from a shared Azure Cosmos DB container to dedicated containers and back to multi-tenancy by default.
The report documents noisy and weak partitions, hot-key throttling, request-tier quality of service, data movement and jointly operated production-scale testing.
visual_brief.editorial_idea: Show isolation, reconnection and a protected priority path as one evolving storage system.
visual_brief.visual_metaphor: partitioned stone blocks connected by movable bridges and a terracotta priority channel
must_show: partitioned stone blocks connected by movable bridges and a terracotta priority channel

candidate_notes.A: Selected: modular blocks, multiple bridges and the priority path express the tenancy trade-off with strong depth and crop resilience.
candidate_notes.B: The circular reservoirs are elegant but make the subject read primarily as water infrastructure.
candidate_notes.C: The movable basins communicate migration but introduce more mechanical detail and weaker thumbnail focus.

crop_review.article_desktop: The priority channel crosses the central field while multiple storage blocks remain visible.
crop_review.article_mobile: The terracotta channel and adjacent partitions survive a central crop.
crop_review.thumbnail: The single priority path remains immediately legible.

golden_reference_comparison: Compared with the two declared repository references for warm paper texture, restrained stone materiality, sparing terracotta emphasis, physical depth and thumbnail legibility. Candidate A was selected after full-size and small-size visual inspection.

generation_metadata.visual_review: Three candidates generated per story. Candidate A was inspected at full size and thumbnail scale; cover-crop safety and prohibited elements were reviewed by Codex model self-review. Candidate C for the Rescale story was rejected for pseudo-text-like paper marks.
